walkthroughs.body_html:
Sound can only travel where there are particles to vibrate.

It travels through solids fastest, then liquids, then gases.

In a vacuum (like space), there's no air - so no sound!

In space, no one can hear you scream - because there's no air to carry the vibration.

Humans hear sounds between 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz.

Lower than 20 Hz = infrasound (elephants use it).
Higher than 20,000 Hz = ultrasound (bats, dolphins, dog whistles).

Sound enters your ear, vibrates your eardrum, and tiny bones send the vibration to your brain.

When sound hits a hard surface, it bounces back. We hear it as an echo.

Ships use sonar: send a sound pulse, time how long the echo takes to return, and calculate the depth.

Bats and dolphins use ultrasound echoes to see their world.

mcqs.q: Why is there no sound in space?
options: Too cold
No light
No particles to vibrate
Too much gravity

mcqs.q: Roughly, what is the human upper hearing limit?
options: 200 Hz

mcqs.q: What is required to induce an emf in a coil using a magnet?
options: Just having a magnet near the coil induces an emf, even when both are stationary.
A current in the coil is what induces an emf in the magnet.
A changing magnetic flux linkage through the coil — the magnet (or coil) must be moving or the field must be changing.
Light-years — it's a measure of cosmic distance.

mcqs.q: What are typical units for the Hubble constant?
options: A current in the coil is what induces an emf in the magnet.
Light-years — it's a measure of cosmic distance.
Metres per second — it's the speed at which the universe expands.
km per second per megaparsec (km/s/Mpc) — recession speed per unit distance.

mcqs.q: An echo takes 4 seconds to return. Sound speed is 340 m/s. How far away is the wall in metres? (Remember: sound travels there and back.)

numericals.q: An echo takes 4 seconds to return. Sound speed is 340 m/s. How far away is the wall in metres? (Remember: sound travels there and back.)
numericals.hint: Total distance = 340 x 4. Then halve for one-way.
